terms.title: Account ID
terms.summary: Identifier for an Iroha account composed of the domain it belongs to and the account controller (single key or multisig policy) that authorizes actions.
terms.tagline: Binds an account to its domain and authorization controller for deterministic identity resolution.

terms.title: Account Lifecycle
terms.summary: The sequence of register, update, rekey, and unregister operations that define how Iroha accounts are created and managed, enforced by on-chain permissions and admission policy.
terms.tagline: Defines how accounts are created, modified, and retired under deterministic on-chain rules.

terms.title: Action
terms.summary: Trigger action payload that bundles the executable, repeats policy, authority, filter, and metadata defining what runs and when.
terms.tagline: Encapsulates the logic, authority, and firing policy behind a trigger.

terms.title: Activation Slot
terms.summary: Scheduled activation height or epoch for staged changes (for example, consensus mode, validator set, or manifest updates) so every node flips at the same block.
terms.tagline: Lets governance stage changes for deterministic activation at a future height.

terms.title: Admission
terms.summary: Torii admission stage that validates transaction envelopes (Norito decode, signatures, chain ID, TTL, size limits) before enqueueing and gossip.
terms.tagline: Rejects malformed or unauthorized transactions at the edge to protect the pipeline.

terms.title: Adoption
terms.summary: Adoption describes the rate at which people, partners, and institutions begin using SORA products, liquidity, and governance tooling in real-world contexts.
terms.tagline: Drives network effects and increases utility for all participants.

terms.title: Aggregation
terms.summary: Oracle aggregation step that combines observations into a consensus value using `AggregationRule` (median/MAD or percentile) after outlier and cap checks.
terms.tagline: Turns multiple oracle reports into a single deterministic feed outcome.

terms.title: Agile Coretime
terms.summary: A flexible market where Polkadot sells coretime slices directly through brokered deals instead of fixed auctions.

terms.title: Algorithmic Stability
terms.summary: Mechanisms that maintain stable asset value through programmatic supply adjustments—core to TBCD and SORA's monetary policy.

terms.title: Analytics

terms.title: Asset Definition ID

terms.title: Asynchronous Backing

terms.title: Attesters
terms.summary: Authorized signers or committees whose keys are configured to issue attestations (for example, DA sampling attesters, fraud monitoring engines, or alias attesters).
terms.tagline: Only attestations from registered attesters are accepted by policy.

terms.title: Parachain Auctions

terms.title: Automation
terms.summary: Deterministic on-chain workflows built with triggers: an executable plus filter and repeat policy that runs on schedules or events.
terms.tagline: Runs recurring or event-driven logic without off-chain bots.

terms.title: Curve25519
terms.summary: The elliptic curve underlying Ed25519 signatures (and X25519 key agreement), used by Iroha's default signature scheme.

terms.title: DA Certificates
terms.summary: Attester-signed certificates that sampled and verified erasure-coded shards for a data space, used by the nexus committee to accept DA without pulling shards.
terms.tagline: Proof that DA sampling succeeded in-slot.

terms.title: DA Sampling
terms.summary: VRF-sampled attesters check a subset of erasure-coded shards each slot and sign availability; sample size and thresholds are deterministic config.
terms.tagline: Randomized shard checks to detect withholding.

terms.title: DA Sampling Budget
terms.summary: Deterministic caps on in-slot DA signatures per lane and per dataspace, plus per-attester shard checks, so sampling work stays bounded.
terms.tagline: Limits DA sampling work per slot.

terms.title: DA Sampling Confidence
terms.summary: The sampling confidence target derived from sample sizes (S) and threshold (T) for DA certificates, controlling how many attester signatures are required.
terms.tagline: Sets how much sampling is enough to accept availability.

terms.title: Data Availability
terms.summary: Erasure-coded Kura/WSV blobs with Merkle commitments in headers; DA attesters sample shards and issue certificates so blocks can commit without downloading full data.
terms.tagline: Commitments plus sampling make blobs retrievable.

terms.title: Data Availability Layer
terms.summary: The DA subsystem: erasure-coded storage, shard sampling, attester certificates, and retrieval policies for public vs private data spaces.
terms.tagline: Provides retrievability for blobs while preserving privacy boundaries.

terms.title: Data Envelope
terms.summary: An ISO 20022 wrapper element (DataEnvelope/DataPDU/Body) that the IVM canonicalizer strips when deriving message paths and hashes.
terms.tagline: Outer ISO 20022 wrapper ignored for canonical paths.

terms.title: Data Space Directory
terms.summary: On-chain registry of Space Directory manifests (AssetPermissionManifest) keyed by UAID and DataSpaceId, with publish/revoke/expire lifecycle.
terms.tagline: Registry of capability manifests per data space.

terms.title: Data Space ID
terms.summary: A 64-bit identifier for a data space; GLOBAL is 0 and IDs can be derived from a stable 32-byte hash.
terms.tagline: Typed identifier for a data space.

terms.title: Data Spaces
terms.summary: Governance buckets that group one or more lanes under shared compliance, routing, and settlement policies; lanes can be public or restricted.
terms.tagline: Groups lanes by policy and governance.

terms.title: Decentralization

terms.tagline: Prevents censorship and ensures permissionless access.

terms.title: Deep-fri

terms.tagline: Low-degree test for STARK-style proofs.

terms.title: Deterministic Runtime

terms.title: Dogecoin (DOGE)
terms.summary: A proof-of-work cryptocurrency launched in 2013 as a Litecoin fork, known for its meme origins and community tipping culture.

terms.title: DSID
terms.summary: Short for DataSpaceId; used in Nexus descriptors and proofs to label which data space a transaction or artifact belongs to.
terms.tagline: Alias for DataSpaceId in Nexus routing and proofs.

terms.title: Economics

terms.title: Ed25519

terms.summary: Energy in SORA context refers to sustainability considerations and the network efficient Proof of Stake consensus, which uses minimal energy compared to Proof of Work systems.

terms.title: Epoch Beacon
terms.summary: A deterministic epoch randomness beacon built by aggregating VRF outputs; inputs bind the epoch number and previous finalized block hash to remove grinding.
terms.tagline: Deterministic VRF beacon per epoch.

terms.title: Erasure-Coded Kura
terms.summary: Kura block bodies stored as erasure-coded blobs with Merkle commitments so public data remains retrievable even after partial shard loss.
terms.tagline: Erasure-coded block storage for retrievability.

terms.title: Erasure-Coded WSV
terms.summary: WSV snapshots are chunked and erasure-coded with commitments recorded in headers; public snapshots are widely sharded while private snapshots stay within permissioned validators.
terms.tagline: Erasure-coded state snapshots with commitments.

terms.title: Execution
terms.summary: The pipeline phase where the on-chain executor (IVM) applies instructions in a StateBlock overlay with deterministic gas metering and syscalls.
terms.tagline: IVM executes instructions deterministically before commit.

terms.title: Exit Caches
terms.summary: SoraNet exit relays and gateways cache recently fetched content keyed by blinded CIDs to reduce repeat fetch latency and smooth egress patterns.
terms.tagline: Exit-side caching to smooth egress and protect privacy.

terms.title: Explorer
terms.summary: Explorer refers to the SORA blockchain explorer experiences that let anyone browse blocks, transactions, governance queues, and validator stats in real time.

terms.title: FASTPQ zk-STARK Proofs

terms.title: Fiat-Shamir Transcript
terms.summary: The hashed conversation log that records each commitment and challenge during proof generation, keeping the prover honest.
terms.tagline: Ensures data integrity and enables secure verification across the network.

terms.title: Fiat-Shamir Transform
terms.summary: The process of converting FASTPQ's interactive protocol into a non-interactive one by hashing prior messages for randomness.
terms.tagline: Ensures data integrity and enables secure verification across the network.

terms.summary: A Polkadot and Kusama feature that lets runtime logic be upgraded without hard forks.

terms.summary: Versioned, audited cost schedules in SORA Nexus assigning deterministic TEU prices to every syscall and instruction, ensuring predictable execution costs across the IVM.

terms.title: Gateways
terms.summary: Stateless admission points accepting signed Norito payloads, applying basic checks, and routing them to the proper data space.
terms.tagline: Simplifies client integration by handling protocol translation and routing.

terms.title: Geo-redundancy
terms.summary: Operational guidance for running validators, provers, and storage nodes across multiple regions to survive localized outages.
terms.tagline: Keeps Nexus online by distributing critical nodes across regions.

terms.title: Goldilocks Field
terms.summary: The 64-bit prime field used by Poseidon2 and FASTPQ in SORA Nexus, chosen because its structure maps efficiently onto modern CPU architectures for fast proof generation.

terms.title: Lambda Exit
terms.summary: The throughput threshold in SORA Nexus that triggers deterministic lane splits when transaction demand exceeds configured capacity, enabling automatic horizontal scaling.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: Lambda Floor
terms.summary: The lower-load threshold that triggers lane fusion when aggregate load drops below this value for two consecutive slots. When the sum of lane loads falls below lambda floor, lanes merge to reduce overhead and improve latency during low-traffic periods.
terms.tagline: Automatically reduces infrastructure overhead when network demand is low.

terms.title: Lane and DA Budgets
terms.summary: The combined constraints on how much transaction work and DA sampling a slot may perform. Lane TEU budgets cap throughput per lane, while DA budgets cap signatures/samples per public data space to keep verification latency predictable.
terms.tagline: Prevents any single lane from starving others of compute resources.

terms.title: Lane Finality
terms.summary: The approximately one-second confirmation target each lane's SUMERAGI pipeline in SORA Nexus reaches before merge ordering combines outputs with other parallel lanes.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing while maintaining global ordering guarantees.

terms.title: Lane Fusion
terms.summary: The deterministic process of collapsing multiple lanes when aggregate load falls below lambda_floor, preserving history.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: Lane Proofs
terms.summary: Aggregated FASTPQ or DA proofs scoped per lane in SORA Nexus, allowing validator committees to verify execution efficiently without processing every transaction individually.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: Lanes
terms.summary: Parallel execution tracks in SORA Nexus that process transactions independently before the Merge Ledger orders their outputs, enabling horizontal scaling without sacrificing global consistency.
terms.tagline: Enables horizontal scaling by running multiple transaction streams concurrently.

terms.title: Lane-Scoped Recovery
terms.summary: SoraNet mechanisms that rebuild state for a single lane without halting the entire network. When a lane experiences issues, the system can recover that lane's WSV and Kura state independently while other lanes continue processing transactions normally, maintaining overall network availability.
terms.tagline: Enables fault isolation so one lane's problems don't affect the entire network.

terms.title: Lane-Scoped State
terms.summary: State shards maintained per lane in SORA Nexus to localize failures and simplify recovery, ensuring that issues in one lane don't cascade across the entire network.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: Lane Split
terms.summary: The process in SORA Nexus of doubling lanes once the lambda_exit threshold is exceeded, enabling automatic horizontal scaling without rewriting transaction history.
terms.tagline: Enables parallel transaction processing for higher throughput.

terms.title: Lane TEU Budget
terms.summary: The per-lane compute allowance (~20,000 TEU/s default) keeping resource usage predictable and fair. TEU budgets work with SFQ scheduling to ensure every data space receives a minimum service level while preventing any single user or application from monopolizing lane capacity.
terms.tagline: Prevents any single lane from starving others of compute resources.

terms.title: Merkle Proof
terms.summary: An inclusion proof that a value is part of a Merkle tree committed by a known root hash, allowing verification without the full dataset.
terms.tagline: Verifies inclusion against a state root with a short authentication path.

terms.title: Mining
